title: Kingdom of Bosnia
capsule: The Kingdom of Bosnia emerged from the elevation of Ban Tvrtko I to king on 26 October 1377, building on a Bosnian realm that had already achieved de facto autonomy under his predecessors. At its height Bosnia controlled much of the western Balkans, with silver mining and caravan trade through Ragusa (Dubrovnik) underpinning its economy, and its nobility exercised substantial power through assemblies called Stanak. Catholic, Bosnian Church, and Orthodox Christian communities coexisted uneasily until the Ottoman conquest on 25 May 1463, when the last king Stephen Tomašević was captured at Jajce and executed; the territory became the westernmost province of the Ottoman Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territory is well established from charter evidence and Ottoman cadastral records, though peripheral zones of contested control with neighboring Dalmatia, Serbia, and Hum are less precisely bounded.
